C9000240.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 240 (Shelah's eventual categoricity and the prescribed-threshold obstruction.; papers: A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold; Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/240.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

C240_UNIFORM.statement: main:uniform: an existential threshold uniform over all AECs with a fixed LS bound, used in both premise and conclusion.

C240_QUALITATIVE.statement: main:qualitative and tail:categoricity: an AEC categorical unboundedly often is categorical on a tail.

C240_DOWNSTREAM_TRANSFER.statement: Sections 4-14 supply pointed uniqueness on a tail and placement of the fixed point pattern in every sufficiently large model. These downstream assertions remain unaudited.

C240_STABLE_DIAGRAMS.statement: Section 4: short strong-map classes stabilize across categoricity sizes; finite supports supply bounded comparison tests, compatible placement, and amalgamation at adequate closed levels.

C240_WORKING_CALCULUS.statement: Sections 5-7: finite working schemes have the required tuple calculus, free extensions, relative isolation, and all-domination with primeness and uniqueness.

C240_MARKED_BOUNDARIES.statement: Sections 8-9: adjoining finite marks preserves the working package, and every finite marked depth admits amalgamated completion and exact boundary isomorphism lifting at adequate levels.

C240_UNIFORM_CODES.statement: close:uniform-definitions: fixed first-order set formulas and a fixed set of descriptors define all finite-depth construction and adequacy requests without invoking a previously selected closure function.

C240_MARKED_COMMON.statement: Section 13, marked application: one sufficiently large eligible level supports every finite marked depth and its exact lifting assertions.

C240_GEOMETRY.statement: Section 10: a minimal singleton type gives a pregeometry; common marked lifting rules out proper no-point-growth extensions, and a downward argument extends this to all sufficiently large pointed models, where basis size equals model size.

C240_GEOMETRIC_BOUNDARIES.statement: Sections 11-12: every finite geometric shape has the working package, classification by prescribed basis maps, and exact boundary lifting at adequate levels.

C240_GEOMETRIC_COMMON.statement: close:common-levels, geometric application: after fixing the no-growth threshold, one level supports all finite geometric shapes and their exact boundary assertions.

C240_CARDINAL_INDUCTION.statement: Section 14: a simultaneous induction on the maximum prescribed basis-piece cardinality for all finite shapes yields pointed categoricity at every sufficiently large cardinal, including limits.

C240_SMALL_CODE.statement: found:small-code: an AEC with LS at most lambda is recoverable, uniformly in set theory, from a set code of its models and strong pairs of size at most lambda.

C240_UNIFORM_REDUCTION.statement: found:uniform-reduction: the qualitative and existential uniform-threshold forms of eventual categoricity are equivalent by Replacement over small codes.

C240_DIRECTED.statement: found:directed-colimits: the AEC chain and coherence axioms give set-indexed directed unions, their common-upper-bound clause, and coherent strong direct limits.

C240_PARTITION.statement: found:partition: each fixed finite-arity coloring has homogeneous subsets of a prescribed cardinality above a sufficiently large cardinal; finitely many arities can be handled together.

C240_ORDER_TEMPLATE.statement: found:order-template: arbitrarily large models yield one functorial finite-support order presentation with at most LS(K) labels and strong subpresentations, of size |I|+LS(K) on infinite orders.

C240_ORDER_BASIC.statement: found:order-basic: H(delta) has size |delta|, point character cf(delta), homogeneous bounded intervals and rays, and finite ordinal-support comparison codes.

C240_BALANCED.statement: found:balanced-cuts: every interior nonprincipal cut of Gamma_delta and H(delta) has equal left and right characters.

C240_CUT_SEGMENTS.statement: found:cut-segments: in the specified homogeneous dense order, a segment approaching a balanced cut of regular character epsilon below the point character has type determined by epsilon, direction, and endpoint.

C240_ORDER_ORBITS.statement: found:order-orbits: for theta<cf(delta), short sequences in H(delta) have the same order-automorphism orbit exactly when their diagrams and all strict-slot occupancies agree.

C240_ORBIT_BOUND.statement: found:orbit-bound: at every categoricity kappa>=max(LS(K),theta^+), including singular kappa, theta-tuple automorphism orbits number at most B=2^(2^(LS(K)+theta)).

C240_PROFILES.statement: The named orbit-arrow relation and partial record-to-name map have a set-sized palette of at most 2^B profiles, uniform in size and presentation ordinal.

C240_SUPPORT_CLOSURE.statement: found:ordinal-support-closure: for theta^+<=a<cf(beta), every at-most-a support set extends to a bounded T0 of size at most a and cofinality above theta, matching every finite ordinal pattern over every at-most-theta subset.

C240_APPEND.statement: found:append-segment: appending a consecutive indecomposable delta after T0 preserves finite-pattern matching over at-most-theta parameters, yields order type delta, and reflects every short H-slot occupancy.

C240_ALIGNMENT.statement: found:alignment: common-profile presentations at a<mu yield a strong a-sized submodel containing any prescribed at-most-a set, with every theta-tuple's small and large orbit names equal.

C240_INDECOMP.statement: found:indecomposable-occurrences: indecomposable ordinals of size kappa and any prescribed infinite regular cofinality tau<=kappa occur cofinally below kappa^+.

C240_COMMON_PROFILE.statement: Unboundedly many failing categoricity sizes yield a<mu with a^theta<=mu, a common cofinally recurring profile, and a mu-presentation ordinal of cofinality greater than a.

C240_PERSISTENCE.statement: An orbit unable to reach p cannot regain reachability under any strong map between mu-sized copies, including the canonical inclusion into every mu-sized limit union.

C240_ELIMINATION.statement: With the common profile and alignment, theta^+ rounds processing all a^theta small tuples force a final a-sized model with no tuple able to reach an orbit p that occurs there, a contradiction.

C240_FORMAL_CORE.statement: Same ordinal-position patterns preserve both coefficient-order levels and all slot inequalities; ordinal cofinality captures short tuples; direct-arrow exclusion persists through arbitrary limits, and the explicit two-scale elimination criterion is contradictory.

C240_REVERSAL.statement: found:reversal: each fixed infinite tuple bound admits reversal at every sufficiently large categoricity cardinal, including singular ones, with no exponentiation or amalgamation assumption.

C240_CH_MAIN.statement: thm:main: under CH, a countable relational AEC with LS aleph_0 is noncategorical at beth_(omega_2) and categorical from beth_((2^(aleph_1))^+) onward.

C240_CH_AEC.statement: Under CH, aec:class: the companion construction satisfies all AEC axioms with LS(K)=aleph_0, including directed unions and smoothness.

C240_CH_ENDPOINT.statement: Under CH, Section 4: rank functions modulo countable sets and coherent countable extensional diagrams produce an uncountable-base object of size beth_(omega_2), distinct from a countable-base object.

C240_CH_DIAGRAMS.statement: Under CH, end:diagrams: the tuplewise countable membership diagrams have exact subsequence restrictions and pass all validity tests outside their countable exceptional sets.

C240_CH_RANK_FUNCTIONS.statement: end:domination: there are functions f_alpha:omega_1->omega_1 for alpha<omega_2 such that gamma<alpha implies f_gamma(beta)<f_alpha(beta) outside a countable set of beta.

C240_CH_COUNTABLE_EXT.statement: end:countable-closures: each nonempty finite subset X of V_(omega_2) lies in a countable extensional membership subdiagram D_X, coherently under nonempty subset inclusions.

C240_CH_NO_PATTERN.statement: Under CH, col:no-pattern: no sequence of one color per finite arity passes every full-subsequence test; its coherent tagged extensional limit would inject too large a set into V_(omega_1).

C240_CH_BOUND.statement: Under CH, cat:bounded: an object with uncountable base has fewer than Lambda=beth_((2^(aleph_1))^+) index points, by the whole-profile palette bound and countably many full-tuple exception sets.

C240_CH_CARDINALS.statement: cat:cardinals: for xi=2^(aleph_1), Lambda=beth_(xi^+) is a strong limit of cofinality xi^+; the finite-arity partition source bounds remain below Lambda.

C240_CH_FINITE_PATTERNS.statement: cat:finite-patterns: colorings of every finite arity on a set of size at least Lambda with palettes of size at most xi admit fixed arity colors realized simultaneously on a separate finite witness at every depth.

C240_CH_COUNTABLE_BASE.statement: For the companion construction under CH, cat:countable-base: two countable-base objects with equally sized index sorts are isomorphic by finite row/column translator allocation.

C240_CH_TAIL.statement: Under CH, cat:tail: models exist at every mu>=Lambda and must have countable base, yielding categoricity via the countable-base classification.
